 This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
1. The claimant is in appeal challenging the exoneration of liability of the insurer and also seeking for enhancement.
2. The Tribunal has exonerated the liability of the insurer on the ground that the offending auto was plying beyond the permit area.

3. In the light of the judgment rendered in the cases of AMRIT PAUL SINGH AND ANOTHER VS TATA AIG GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND OTHERS - 2018 7 SCC 558 AND RANI AND OTHERS VS NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD. AND OTHERS - 2018 8 SCC 492, this ground will be no avail to the insurer and consequently, the finding of the Tribunal that the insurer would not be liable is set aside and it is held that the insurer is liable to pay the compensation.
4.

In order to arrive at the said conclusion, the Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 8%
and has determined the notional income at Rs.7,000/- per month.
Since the doctor who treated the claimant has stated that the claimant had suffered 12% disability to whole body, the reduction of the disability to 8% cannot be sustained.

Consequently, it is held that the petitioner had suffered 12%
disability to whole body.
6. As far as income is concerned, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.7,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income,
it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2017, would be Rs.11,000/-.
7. As the claimant was aged 35 years, a multiplier of '16' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,53,440/- (Rs.11,000/- x 12 x 16 x 12%) towards 'loss of future income'.

8. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.10,000/-
towards 'loss of amenities and enjoyment of life'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of amenities and enjoyment of life'.
9. The sum of Rs.94,325/- awarded towards 'medical expenses' is just and proper and is affirmed.
10. The claimant was hospitalized for nine days.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards 'food, diet, nourishment and attendant charges'.
As the claimant was hospitalized for nine days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.15,000/- on this account.
11. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as two months.

Since the claimant has suffered 36%
disability to the particular limb, it would be appropriate to treat the laid up period as three months Thimmaraju vs Lakshmikantha P on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167649370/
